clue.text: Greek love to consume beef

definitions.note: to beef is slang for to complain, a verb here

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the round letter O
to consume something is to use it up

explanation.surface: A Greek lover is about to tuck into some beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' reads as meat but is the verb meaning to complain or grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for complaining or moaning about something.

clue.text: Colourful swimmer — like a coelacanth, say, with head of gudgeon

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the start of the fish named

parts.note: the coelacanth is an ancient 'living fossil', so it is an aged swimmer

explanation.surface: Describing a bright aquarium fish by comparing it with prehistoric species.
explanation.walkthrough: A coelacanth is a fish once thought extinct for millions of years, so it is an 'old fish'; put G in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental carp kept in bowls is bright orange, a vividly coloured pet fish.

clue.text: Think too highly of settled price?

parts.note: a matter that is settled is finished, done and over
a rate is a price charged, as in hourly rate

explanation.surface: Asking whether an agreed price shows someone valued something too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To overvalue is to give something more credit or worth than it deserves.

clue.text: Robbery can be a bit of a strain

explanation.surface: A theft might be a little stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress but means a tune: a snatch is a short fragment of song.
explanation.definitionFit: A grab-and-run theft is a robbery; a brief fragment of melody is a short piece of a tune.

clue.text: Farm butter charges, his?

parts.note: an animal on a farm that butts with its horns, a billy or nanny
the animals in someone's care, his charges, form a flock or drove

explanation.surface: A question about who looks after the head-butting animals on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not dairy produce but one who butts; the whole clue asks whose charges these butting animals are, and the man who tends them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural worker who tends a flock of nannies and billies is called by this name.

clue.text: University way to expel

parts.note: the OU is Britain's Open University
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A university's method of throwing someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University (OU) is a British distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or drive someone out of a place or position.

clue.text: Old aircraft's flight over country road

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second in the column

parts.note: a flight is a journey, a trip
a lane is a narrow country road

explanation.surface: An early plane flies above a rural road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places TRIP above LANE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-winged aeroplane, a design of the First World War era now obsolete.

clue.text: Wanton sex lie can produce outcasts

indicators.note: wanton means unruly or undisciplined, so these letters run wild

explanation.surface: Sexual misconduct and lying can get people banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanton' signals that the letters of SEX LIE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: People banished from their homeland are rejected and cast out by society.

clue.text: Arabic characters understand it is abbreviated

parts.note: to dig is slang for to understand
it is shortens to it's, giving these three letters

explanation.surface: A remark about following abbreviations written in Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabic characters' are not Arabic letters but numerals such as 1, 2, 3.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerals 0 to 9 are written with figures called Arabic numerals.

clue.text: General method of play

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A commander's tactics for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is not a game but slack or room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom of movement or slack in a mechanism or rule is room for manoeuvre.

clue.text: Ambitious, takes headache cure to onset of grippe

parts.note: aspirin is a common painkiller for headaches

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get ahead takes a pill at the first sign of flu.
explanation.walkthrough: Grippe is an old word for influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving towards a goal, eager for success.

clue.text: Poe's new custom, to embrace a cause

indicators.note: making the letters new means forming them into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the writer's name without the possessive mark
a use is a habitual practice or custom

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe adopts a new habit of championing causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges POES into ESPO; then add USE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt or support a belief or movement.

clue.text: Prediction is a warning, of course, to players

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout on a golf course
the actors in a play form its cast

explanation.surface: A forecast as a caution given to a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to a golf course, where 'fore!' warns of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather outlook or estimate of what will happen.

clue.text: A pound tie can be knotted, though

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

indicators.note: a tie that is knotted is twisted around, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tie worth a pound can still be tied in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be knotted' rearranges TIE into EIT, after A and LB.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning even though, although.

clue.text: Sensationally, Mediterranean island seizes power

indicators.note: seizing something means holding it in, so the island wraps around the letter

parts.note: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A dramatic news report of a coup on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A racy, titillating way of telling something is a hot, spiced-up manner.

clue.text: Variety of teas satisfy

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Different kinds of tea quench a thirst.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill completely or gratify an appetite.

clue.text: House guests?

explanation.surface: Asking who is staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a business firm, not a home; visitors are also called company.
explanation.definitionFit: A business firm is called a house; visitors in your home keep you company.

clue.text: Poor stock brings ill-will

explanation.surface: Inferior breeding leads to hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior lineage is literally a tainted bloodline; hostility between people is resentment.

clue.text: Name girl coming out to sidestep

indicators.note: letters coming out of their places are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl named at her debut avoids something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' rearranges the letters of NAME GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign illness so as to dodge work is to avoid duty.

clue.text: Hole crab made for a young seal

indicators.note: something made is newly built, here from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A crab digs a hole for a baby seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges HOLE CRAB; a young male fur seal without a mate is called a bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists call a young male fur seal that has no harem by this term.

clue.text: Hurried to fire rifle

parts.note: to have hurried is to have run
to sack is to dismiss, to fire someone

explanation.surface: Rushed off to shoot a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is the verb to search through and plunder, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a place is to plunder or search it roughly.

clue.text: This adventure, a sensation on the way back?

indicators.note: travelling back means the whole phrase is read from right to left

parts.note: a gas is informal for a sensation, a great thrill

explanation.surface: An adventure story about a thrill on the homeward journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns the whole of A GAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic tale of adventure, originally Norse.

clue.text: Embarrassed, coming out of purdah?

indicators.note: letters coming out of a word are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman emerging from seclusion feels awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' means financially embarrassed, short of money. Purdah is the seclusion of women in some cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: Being financially embarrassed is being short of cash.

clue.text: Run counter to cook fried head of fish

indicators.note: 'to' puts one piece inside the other
to cook figures is to falsify them, so these letters are fiddled
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe: fry a fish head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges FRIED into DIFER, then F, the first letter of fish, completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree or be unlike is to go against something.

clue.text: Sock box?

explanation.surface: Asking whether to punch someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock or box someone is to hit them with a blow.

clue.text: Defiant disposition of arms

parts.note: reads as a military stance of weapons but means the defiant pose with hands on hips

explanation.surface: A rebellious deployment of weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' are limbs, not weapons: hands on hips, elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands on hips with elbows turned outward is a challenging posture.

clue.text: Low angle of ray, possibly

parts.note: a flat note or level is low
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A low-angled beam of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' is the sea creature, not a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays, plaice and sole are examples of fish with flattened bodies.

clue.text: Be late for girl

explanation.surface: Running late for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to catch a train is to arrive too late; a young unmarried woman is addressed this way.

clue.text: One of the lakeside dancers in lines

definitions.text: One of the lakeside dancers in lines

parts.words: One of the lakeside dancers in lines
parts.note: recalls Wordsworth's poem, in lines of verse, about yellow flowers dancing beside the lake

explanation.surface: A member of a chorus line dancing by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud' describes golden flowers 'beside the lake... dancing in the breeze'; 'lines' are lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flowers of the poem are described as dancing.

clue.text: Hebridean caveman?

parts.note: points to the famous sea cave on Staffa, named after a legendary hero

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man from the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Fingal's Cave is a sea cave on Staffa in the Inner Hebrides, named after the giant hero of Ossian; so he is the 'man' of the cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary giant gives his name to a celebrated cavern on a western Scottish isle.

clue.text: One who sends up tripod, as ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, here the letters

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a camera stand as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges TRIPOD AS; 'sends up' means mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mocks by imitation, a satirist or lampooner.

clue.text: Shock from geologist's last fault

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: an error is a fault or mistake

explanation.surface: A geologist's final fault line causes an earthquake shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' looks like a geological fault but is just a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fear or fright is a jolt of dread.
